title: Sqrt(x)
summary: You get a non-negative integer `x`. Return the largest integer whose square is at most `x`: the square root of `x` with any fractional part dropped. Built-in shortcuts are off limits, so use no square root or power function and no `**` operator.

examples.explanation: 5 × 5 = 25 is at most 30, but 6 × 6 = 36 is more than 30.

constraints: Your method must run in O(log x) time

approaches.twist: Binary search over the candidate answers 0 to x: square the middle guess, and keep the largest one whose square is at most x.
Count up from 0 and return the last number whose square is still at most x.
approaches.note: Works, but counting up takes about √x steps, over 46,000 when x is near 2³¹. The target is O(log x).

signals.phrase: largest integer whose square is at most
signals.meaning: Search on the answer: every integer up to the answer has a square that fits, and every larger one doesn't. Square a middle guess and keep the half where the answer can be.
The size here is the value x, not a length. log x means halving the range of possible answers, 0 to x, about 31 times.

signals.phrase: no square root or power function
signals.meaning: You can't call math.isqrt, so you have to find the root yourself. Testing a guess needs only one multiplication.

constraintReading: Here n is the value x itself, up to 2³¹ − 1, about 2.1·10⁹. Trying every number up to x is far too slow, and even counting up to √x, O(√n), takes over 46,000 steps. The O(log x) requirement means halving the range 0 to x instead: about 31 steps, with O(1) space.

related.relation: Also searches over possible answers instead of indexes, testing each guess with a quick calculation.
